  nThe curve has two peaks
  nBritish land snails vary because a wide geographic range causes selection to vary
explanation: Disruptive selection occurs when environmental conditions favor individuals at both extremes of a phenotypic range over individuals with intermediate phenotypes. This splits the distribution curve, creating two distinct peaks. The slide provides the example of British land snails, where phenotypic variation is maintained because a wide geographic range results in varying local selection pressures, favoring different shell patterns in different habitats.

questions.q: Which selection type is characterized by a distribution curve with two distinct peaks?
questions.exp: Disruptive selection favors multiple extreme phenotypes, resulting in a distribution curve with two peaks.

questions.q: Why do British land snails exhibit disruptive selection?
opts: They do not experience natural selection.
A wide geographic range causes environmental selection pressures to vary, favoring different phenotypes.
They mate assortatively based on body size only.
questions.exp: The notes state that British land snails vary because their wide geographic range causes selection pressures to vary, which promotes multiple favored phenotypes (peaks) in the population.
